Title: June 4, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting (Joint Public Hearing with Planning Board on Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan Major Update)

Topic1.Title: Pride Month Declaration and Proclamation Remarks
Topic1.Summary: Mayor Brockett read a declaration commemorating June 2026 as Pride Month, honoring the Stonewall legacy and Boulder's LGBTQ+ community. Representatives from Rocky Mountain Equality spoke in response and thanked the council. Councilmember Mark gave a point of personal privilege condemning a student group's statement about a June 2025 attack, and the district attorney's statement was also read into the record.

Topic2.Title: Consent Agenda Approval
Topic2.Summary: Council considered consent agenda items 2A through 2F, which covered several routine items. A motion and second were made, and the consent agenda was approved unanimously on a roll call vote.

Topic3.Title: Joint Public Hearing Opening and Staff Presentation on Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan Update
Topic3.Summary: Staff introduced the recommended major update to the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan, which was developed over about 20 months with more than 70 engagement opportunities and over a thousand comments. Presenters outlined goals for inclusive process, values-based approach, 104 usable policies, and a simplified 12-designation future land use strategy. Highlights included equity, housing supply, mobility, economic vitality, natural resources, Vision Zero, climate resilience, and city-county governance.

Topic4.Title: Approval Process, Review Roles and Schedule
Topic4.Summary: Christopher Johnson explained that four bodies must approve the identical plan, with the city council and planning board handling all policies and map changes and county bodies reviewing county-related items. Council and planning board will deliberate separately on June 16 and June 25, with a county joint hearing on June 11. Any substantive amendments must be reconciled across all bodies, which could extend the timeline into summer or fall.

Topic5.Title: Council Questions on Land Use Map Changes, Maintenance Funding and Wildfire-Area Density
Topic5.Summary: Council asked for a delta map showing land use changes since the last draft, and staff agreed to prepare one for the June 16 meeting. Council members raised concerns about funding for long-term facility maintenance and affordable housing targets, and staff pointed to updated policies on asset maintenance and funding. Questions about increasing density near the wildland-urban interface led staff to explain that rezoning and public review would be needed before any such increase.

Topic6.Title: Questions on Industrial Land Use, Residential Uses and Displacement Concerns
Topic6.Summary: Council members asked whether residential uses are prohibited in industrial designations and whether existing industrial businesses would be protected from displacement. Staff explained that zoning still governs allowed uses, that site review is more discretionary than use review, and that existing industrial tenants have limited protections under the plan. Staff noted that the plan aims to create housing elsewhere to reduce pressure on industrial land.

Topic7.Title: Questions on Affordable Housing Goal, Implementation and Indigenous Partnership
Topic7.Summary: Council asked why the plan keeps a 15 percent affordable housing goal, and staff said the goal is aspirational and was set to be ambitious. Members asked how the plan will move from policy to action, and staff pointed to the upcoming citywide strategic plan and council priority setting. A council member raised the need for stronger commitments to indigenous communities, including land back.

Topic8.Title: Questions on Planning Areas, Subcommunity Planning, Groundwater and Process for Proposed Amendments
Topic8.Summary: Council and planning board members questioned how amendments should be submitted, with staff advising that suggestions go to staff rather than through a public hotline to avoid serial meetings. Members asked about the future of subcommunity and area planning guidance, the IGA for the Area 3 planning reserve, and groundwater protection, which the state regulates. Staff confirmed the IGA runs through 2042 and will be revisited.

Topic9.Title: Public Hearing Procedures and Public Testimony
Topic9.Summary: Alicia read the public participation guidelines, and 17 speakers signed up with two-minute limits. Speakers raised concerns about land use designations changing residential and industrial zones, housing types and density, middle-income housing, notification of property owners, the survey's design, water supply and wildfire risk, and the process used to develop the plan. Some speakers supported the plan and its inclusive process and called for restoring residential uses in industrial designations.

Topic10.Title: Clarifying Questions on Notification, Survey Methods and Outreach Demographics
Topic10.Summary: Staff explained that property owners were notified through a utility billing insert because mailing 55,000 letters was not feasible, and the city attorney confirmed legal notice requirements were met. Staff said the survey was developed with a national consultant, and clarified that outreach was open to all residents without a specific 25 percent focus on college students. Council members also asked about how outreach reached renters and homeowners.

Topic11.Title: Planning Board Continuance Motion
Topic11.Summary: The planning board chair asked for a motion to continue the item to June 16, 2026, for planning board deliberation and action. The motion was made and seconded, and it passed seven to zero. No additional public comment will be taken at that meeting, though emails will be read.

Topic12.Title: Council Continuance Motion and Adjournment
Topic12.Summary: Council moved to continue the item to June 25, 2026, for council deliberation and action on the plan, with no additional public comment at that meeting. The motion was seconded and passed unanimously. The mayor thanked staff and planning board members and adjourned the meeting.
